app.sense: A program on the Mac (another app, the app itself), as a common noun.

cursor.sense: The file-list cursor: the highlighted row the keyboard acts on (also the viewer's text cursor).

git-branch.sense: A git branch, as the git portal and the git status chip show it.

git-commit.sense: A git commit (a snapshot in the repo's history), as the git portal lists it.

internet.sense: The internet as a whole, mostly in "check your internet connection" advice.

key-combination.sense: The actual keys pressed together that a shortcut is bound to (the thing a shortcut conflict is about).

mac.sense: The user's computer, named as a Mac ("on this Mac", "stays on your Mac").
mac.note: Apple's own prose names the machine with a classifier in several languages; keep "Mac" itself verbatim.

network.sense: A computer network in general (the Network group in the volume switcher, network drives, network errors).

open-beta.sense: Cmdr's public beta phase, named in onboarding, the About window, and the analytics setting.

pattern.sense: A name or text pattern the user types (a glob or regex in search and selection, a rename pattern).

recent.sense: Recently used or newest items (recent searches, the most recent download).

regex.sense: A regular expression as a search or selection mode.

repository.sense: A git repository Cmdr detects and shows through its git portal and status chip.
repository.note: English uses both the short "repo" and the full "repository"; a locale may mirror that register split.

reset.sense: Putting a setting, zoom level, or shortcut back to its default value.

status.sense: The state an item or connection is in (a status column, a status dot, a status badge).

subscription.sense: A recurring paid commercial license (as opposed to a perpetual one).

technical-details.sense: The disclosure in an error dialog that shows the raw system error, which suggestion text points at.
